commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: Align with AB3 template and v1.4
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide has no Acknowledgements section, and most of its
implementation notes have no design considerations. Its use cases do
not follow the AB3 format, some requirements are inaccurate, and its
manual tests repeat the same index checks for every command.

The tP requires an accurate Acknowledgements section, and evaluators
compare the DG against the AB3 template and the latest release.

Let's update the DG, keeping the v1.4 content that is already there:

* Restore the Acknowledgements section
* Add implementation sections, with design considerations, for nested
  indexes, gig editing, safe deletion, cross-client views, and the
  summary
* Restore the proposed undo/redo design and add a proposed data
  archiving design
* Rewrite the user stories, use cases, NFRs, and glossary in the AB3
  format, and label unimplemented user stories as planned
* Lower the capacity NFR to 1000 gigs and payment obligations, as the
  app has not been tested with 5000
* Add manual tests for summary, and test index validation only once
* Add an Effort appendix

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor code to follow Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Checkstyle passes, but it does not check some parts of the Java
coding standard (intermediate). Several booleans do not read as
true/false statements, the same invalid gig and payment index
messages are defined in up to 8 commands, and a few methods mix
several steps. Many tests also check several groups of inputs without
saying which group each case belongs to, which makes them harder to
review and grade.

Let's align the code with the standard, without changing behavior:

* Rename booleans to read as statements, e.g. CommandResult's
  shouldShowHelp() and shouldExit(), and PaymentObligation's isPaid.
  The saved JSON key "paid" is unchanged.
* Move MESSAGE_INVALID_GIG_INDEX and MESSAGE_INVALID_PAYMENT_INDEX
  into Messages
* Split SummaryCommand#execute, MainWindow#executeCommand, and
  GigabyteData#matchReplacementGigIndexes into named steps
* Wrap lines close to the 120-character limit
* Make @TempDir fields package-private
* Label equivalence partitions and boundary values in tests, and split
  mixed invalid-input tests into one test per input group

The public value fields inherited from AB3, such as Name#fullName and
Phone#value, are kept as an accepted template exception.

commitResults.messageTitle: SummaryCommand: Add header comments to private helpers
Tag: Limit tag names to 25 characters
commitResults.messageBody:
Tag names accept any number of alphanumeric characters. A very long
tag, such as one over 1000 characters, cannot be viewed properly in
the client list.

Let's reject tags longer than 25 characters in add and edit, and
document the limit in the User Guide.

The limit is not applied when loading the data file. A stricter load
check would make an older file with a long tag invalid, so Gigabyte
would start with an empty client list and overwrite the file on the
next save.

commitResults.messageTitle: FilterGigsCommand: Use singular gig for one match
commitResults.messageBody:
The gigs command always reports the count with the plural word, so
a filter with exactly one match shows "1 gigs with status COMPLETED."

Let's use "gig" when the count is 1 and "gigs" otherwise, as
OutstandingCommand already does for payment obligations.
style(ui): brighten contrast of background texts

GigabyteParser matches command words exactly, so LIST, List and AddGig
are rejected as unknown commands. The PE guidance treats keywords that
are case-sensitive for no reason as a feature flaw.

Let's lower-case the command word with Locale.ROOT before matching it.
All COMMAND_WORD constants are already lower case. Arguments are left
as typed, so names, titles and keywords keep their case.

Let's also note in the UG command-format notes that command words are
not case-sensitive.

The clear command replies "Address book has been cleared!", which is
left over from AddressBook-Level3. Gigabyte has no address book, and
the message does not say that gigs and payment obligations are deleted
too, which matters for a destructive command.

Let's say exactly what was removed: "Cleared all clients, gigs, and
payment obligations." The Developer Guide's manual test for clear is
updated to expect the new message.

The deadlines command ignores any input after the command word, so
'deadlines unexpected' shows the overview instead of an error. This is
inconsistent with outstanding, which rejects extra input.

Let's reject extra input for deadlines the same way.

* Add a MESSAGE_USAGE to DeadlinesCommand
* Extract the existing outstanding check into
  GigabyteParser#requireNoArguments and use it for both commands
* Update the UG and DG to list which no-parameter commands ignore
  extra input and which reject it
